function.name: calculate_investment_value
function.description: Calculate the future value of an investment given the principal, interest rate and term. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

principal.description: The initial amount of the investment. This is a float type value.

interest_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. Enter as a decimal (for 5%, enter 0.05). This is a float type value.

term.description: The term of the investment in years.

compounding.description: The number of times that interest is compounded per year. Default is 1 (annually).

message.content:
Sure! Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1960 | *Psycho* | Alfred Hitchcock | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | *Halloween* | John Carpenter | The original slasher that set the genre’s template. |
| 1980 | *The Shining* | Stanley Kubrick | A chilling psychological horror with iconic imagery. |
| 1984 | *A Nightmare on Elm Street* | Wes Craven | Freddy’s first appearance and a fresh take on supernatural fear. |
| 1999 | *The Sixth Sense* | M. Night Shyamalan | A twisty thriller that keeps you guessing until the end. |
| 2002 | *28 Days Later* | Danny Boyle | A post‑apocalyptic horror that revitalized the zombie genre. |
| 2004 | *Saw* | James Wan | A gritty, puzzle‑based horror that sparked a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | *Paranormal Activity* | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage that made audiences jump out of their seats. |
| 2010 | *The Conjuring* | James Wan | A modern supernatural horror that blends scares with a strong narrative. |
| 2012 | *The Cabin in the Woods* | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | *It Follows* | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh, creepy premise that feels both retro and contemporary. |
| 2016 | *Get Out* | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that’s as smart as it is scary. |
| 2018 | *Hereditary* | Ari Aster | A slow‑burning, deeply unsettling psychological horror. |
| 2020 | *Midsommar* | Ari Aster | A daylight horror that turns the genre on its head. |
| 2021 | *The Invisible Man* | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling that mixes sci‑fi with psychological dread. |
| 2023 | *Evil Dead Rise* | Lee Cronin | A fresh entry in the franchise that’s both gory and inventive. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—whether you like psychological thrillers, supernatural chills, or slasher classics. Happy watching!
